chunks: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ja'far al-Asadi narrated to us from Sahl b. Ziyad al-Adami from Ya'qub b. Yazid from Muhammad b. Hamza from one who heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say:
Whoever meets a pilgrim and shakes his hand is like one who touched the [Black] Stone.

key_terms.استلم: Istilam: the ritual act of touching or kissing the Black Stone during Hajj
key_terms.الحجر: The [Black] Stone (al-Hajar al-Aswad), set in the corner of the Ka'ba
key_terms.حاجًّا: A pilgrim (hajj), one who has performed the pilgrimage to Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for shaking hands with a returning pilgrim in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) teaches that greeting a returning pilgrim warmly by shaking hands earns the greeter a spiritual reward comparable to touching the Black Stone during Hajj. This hadith, delivered in the assembly of Rajab 368 AH, emphasizes the communal dimension of pilgrimage and how the blessings of Hajj extend beyond the pilgrim to those who receive them with respect.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ja`far al-Asadi narrated to us from Sahl b. Ziyad al-Adami from Ya`qub b. Yazid from Muhammad b. Hamza from him who heard Aba `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as) say:
He who meets a pilgrim and makes room for him shall be like one who reached the [Black] Stone.
